# Workflow and publication instructions

This file applies to `.github/**`. Read the root policy first. Workflow work that changes repository gates or harness behavior must also read `scripts/AGENTS.md`; changes to public release claims must read `docs/AGENTS.md`. Use rule IDs for those cross-scope references instead of copying their text.

## Owned invariant

<!-- OW-RULE:I50 -->
50. Daily previews, release candidates, and stable promotion are separate transactions. The scheduled daily preview builds one source-derived, non-release identity from protected `main`, retains its VSIX/checksum/provenance triple for 14 days, and never creates a tag, GitHub Release, registry publication, or promotable candidate. A manual first-attempt release-candidate dispatch from protected `main` validates stable metadata, runs the authoritative source contract, packages exactly one canonical triple, and reuses its numeric artifact ID across bounded macOS/Windows, Linux VS Code, one pinned Cursor lifecycle seam, R 4.4/4.5, installed-performance, released/remote Jupyter, and Remote SSH acceptance without rebuilding. Every consumer freshly revalidates checksum, provenance, and archive semantics immediately before use; every `always()` fan-in accepts only exact `success` results. The read-only qualification run retains that triple and one bounded manifest for 21 days and the path-free performance report for 90 days. Stable promotion accepts only a candidate run ID and matching stable tag. Its read-only selector requires a successful first-attempt candidate completed 168–336 hours earlier, rejects expired or missing artifacts and any newer successful candidate for the same tag, and returns exact numeric artifact IDs plus the historical source SHA. Only the protected `publishing` job receives `contents: write`; it checks out that historical source, downloads the exact artifacts from the exact run, verifies the manifest, performance report, source, checksum, provenance, and VSIX bytes, and never builds or packages. It then creates or verifies the lightweight tag and draft-first immutable GitHub Release, publishes the identical bytes to Open VSX, and lets the real tag trigger the separately protected Azure Marketplace pipeline. All GitHub public mutation owners share the non-cancelling `openwrangler-release-publication` queue with `queue: max`; neither registry path may rebuild, rewrite, or substitute the VSIX, and both must verify public bytes after publication. Failed candidates are never retried or promoted. Historical 1.99.x preview inspectors remain available only for exact recovery; there is no current preview-publication entry point. Remote SSH may upload no raw, globbed, or private-state diagnostics while its runner lacks the sealed invariant-40 evidence receipt.
